dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hello, yes, good afternoon. My name is Neusa Pina. I'm calling because there's a tree down, in the park, and I don't know who you tell about that.
Okay, Ms. Pina, I can help with that. A tree down in a park. Which park is it, do you know?

Well, it's the little park near me, not the big one. I'm at 207 Kingston Avenue, up on the Hill, and I walk over there most mornings, or I did, my knee has been something this fall. My sister used to say the knee is the weather report. Anyway. I went over this morning and there's a big limb, no, the whole tree, it's laying across the path.
The whole tree is across the path. And you're at 207 Kingston Avenue, that's what I have. Is the park right on Kingston, or is it on a side street?

It's down the end of the street, maybe a block, the one with the benches and the old stone wall. I never remember what they call it. The wall was there when I came here, that's more years than I want to count.
That's all right, a block down from you with the benches and the stone wall, we can work with that. When do you think it came down?

It was the storm. The nor'easter, Friday and Saturday, three days ago now. I was there Thursday and it was standing. Sunday I didn't go, because of the wind still and the church, and then Monday it rained. So this morning, Tuesday, I saw it. So it came down in the storm, I'd say.
Okay, so it was standing Thursday and you found it down this morning, after the nor'easter Friday and Saturday. Is anyone hurt, or is it on a building or a car or any wires?

No, no one hurt, nobody was there. No cars. There are wires on the street side, the poles, but the tree is on the grass and the path. I didn't see it touching wires. I stayed back, I'm not going close, I have my cane.
Good, that's smart to stay back. And my question to you, so I send it to the right place, is it a city park, do you know, or could it be private property?

That's what I'm asking you, really. Who does it? Is it the city, or the owner, or the electric company? Because my neighbor says call National Grid, and the man at the corner store says it's the city, and I said I'll just call and find out. Who do I call about a downed tree?

You called the right place for a city park. If it's a city park or on a city street, Public Works or the Parks people handle it, and I can take the report right now. If it's on private land, the owner handles it. And if a tree is on wires, that goes to the utility. From what you describe, a park with a path, it sounds like the city, so I'll write it up that way.
Good, good. Because I didn't want to call the wrong one and have them tell me no. That happened with my landlord, you know, with the back steps, three people and nobody's job.

Oh, that's the worst. So let me get this down. A large tree fully down across the walking path, in the small park about a block from 207 Kingston Avenue, with benches and a stone wall, came down in the storm over the weekend. No injuries, no known contact with wires. Did I get that right?
Yes, that's right. Across the path, the whole thing. It's a big one, the trunk is as wide as, as my kitchen table, I'd say. Maybe not the whole table. A card table.
A big trunk, got it. Is the path blocked completely, or can people walk around it on the grass?
They could walk around on the grass, but it's soggy there. Somebody older could slip. The ground has been wet since Saturday. I'd say it's blocked for me anyway.

Okay, blocked for walkers, wet ground around it. I'll note that. I can't tell you the exact day a crew will get there, they've got a lot of storm calls right now, but it goes in the list with the park location.
Oh, I understand, they're busy. Everybody had trees, I saw on the news. There was one on Bellevue too, I think, or my niece said. Not my niece, my friend's niece. It doesn't matter.
That's fine. If you want, I can also have someone call you back if they need more detail on where the park is. Is the best number 401-555-0189?

Yes, that's the house phone. 401-555-0189. I'm usually home, afternoons especially. Mornings I'm at the park, when I can be, or at the pharmacy. If I'm not picking up, let it ring, it takes me a minute to get to it.
Will do, I'll note to let it ring. 401-555-0189, Neusa Pina, at 207 Kingston Avenue. Is it Neusa, N-E-U-S-A?
Yes, N-E-U-S-A. And Pina, P-I-N-A. People put an extra N in it, or an H. It's not hard, but people want it to be.
P-I-N-A, got it. Anything else about the tree I should add, or any other hazard you saw over there?

Well, there's a branch on the sidewalk on Kingston too, a smaller one, in front of the yellow house. But that one you can step over. I'd not call it a problem. Oh, and my landlord, since I mentioned him. He's putting the rent up in the spring. He sent the letter. So I'm thinking about what to do, stay or look somewhere smaller. I'm not asking you about that, I'm just, it's on my mind, with the park being the reason I like the street.

I understand. That's a decision for you to sort out, I'm sorry I can't help on that one from here. I'll add the small branch on the Kingston sidewalk in front of the yellow house to the report as well, as a lower priority.
Yes, that's fine. Put it as small. I don't want them thinking it's the same as the big one.

I'll make that clear. So to repeat it back: a big tree down across the path in the park near the stone wall and benches, about a block from you, from the weekend nor'easter, plus a small branch on the Kingston sidewalk. Public Works will pass it to the right crew, and if they have questions they'll call 401-555-0189.
That's it exactly. Thank you very much, Lorraine. You were patient with me, I know I go around the block before I get to the corner.
No trouble at all, Ms. Pina. Take care on that wet ground, and stay clear of the tree until the crew has been.
I will. Thank you. Goodbye.
Goodbye now.
